findings: Both captures are a multicountry directory for institution and destination support by country and rail for eligible Stripe users, with a local-currency requirement (old raw lines 4–21 and 8719–8721, new raw lines 5–20 and 8639–8641). Select the country and check its applicable debit-card or bank-account section, which distinguishes support for all versus some cards/accounts. The directory establishes destination-selection guidance and no payout lifecycle transition.

The November directory flattens expandable sections into inline tables, drops repetitive third-level labels, normalizes Markdown padding and table rules, and shows a literal star rather than an escaped Markdown star in the otherwise unchanged US E*Trade Bank entry (old raw lines 12–22, 1369–1371; new raw lines 13–21, 1368–1370; diff lines 1363 and 7019). Apart from the dated row changes separately recorded, these changes are presentational.

Baseline summary line 65 mislabels the May directory as a US lookup. Both captures extend past the US and include Canadian Visa or PLUS debit cards, UK bank accounts limited to institutions using Faster Payments (with the Pay.UK sort-code checker) and account guidance for applicable EU sections using the modal 'should' for receiving SEPA Instant Payments (old raw lines 6569–6577, 6805–6807, 7255–7257; new raw lines 6567–6574, 6795–6797, 7231–7233). Current summary line 49 also broadens the May guide's 'European Union (Euro Area)' group to 'EU', which overlaps the debit-card-only countries in line 50. The May guide raw lines 197–205 explicitly distinguishes those groups and routes to this directory.
substantive_changes: US account directory adds Lead Bank in the 'Some accounts' category, between Lea County State Bank and Ledyard National Bank (old raw lines 6254–6261, new raw lines 6252–6260, diff line 12799). This is newly documented row coverage in the November 7 capture.

The Germany debit-card listing changes the N26 GMBH row from 'All debit cards' to 'Some debit cards' (old raw lines 7215–7221, new raw lines 7191–7197, diff lines 14308 and 14384). The qualification is specific to the Germany debit-card row, not the German bank-account section or every N26 listing.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain both May 11 and November 7, 2026 as dated institution snapshots, including the earlier Germany N26 GMBH all-debit-cards label and the newer some-debit-cards label. Retain the separate May main guide and advance-funding provenance at current source lines 6–9 and 62–66.

Retain the country and currency prerequisites, all/some distinction, Canadian Visa/PLUS qualification, UK Faster Payments and conditional EU SEPA Instant guidance (old raw lines 8–10, 5671–5677, 6569–6577, 6805–6807, 7255–7257; new raw lines 9–11, 5670–5675, 6567–6574, 6795–6797, 7231–7233). Keep the independent eligibility route separate from the institution lookup.

Preserve the existing summary-to-Stripe Payouts concept route (current source lines 57–66) and reciprocal concept-to-summary link (concept lines 48–52 and 80–90). The two dated directory captures belong on the source's raw evidence route.
conflicts: The generic introduction says only listed institutions support Instant Payouts, while the UK and applicable EU account sections supply rail-based guidance and external reference links instead of exhaustive account tables (old raw lines 8–10, 6805–6807 and 7255–7257; new raw lines 9–11, 6795–6797 and 7231–7233). Preserve those country-specific qualifications.

Both captures list the same exact label Bank of America N.A. under both 'All accounts' and 'Some accounts' in the US Accounts table (old raw lines 5687 and 5953; new raw lines 5684 and 5950). The institution label alone cannot resolve eligibility for the particular account.
The existing source's broad EU method label and US-only lookup label are baseline scope issues (current source lines 47–51 and 62–66), independent of the two November row deltas.
unresolved_questions: The US account table gives no basis to reconcile its duplicate Bank of America N.A. labels or determine which particular Lead Bank accounts or German N26 debit cards qualify. The captures do not verify individual Stripe user eligibility or live destination acceptance.

answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/instant-payouts-banks is Stripe’s institution-support directory for eligible Instant Payout users. In both captures the user selects a country and checks the destination type, including all-versus-some debit card or bank account distinctions, and must use the local currency. The Canadian list is for Visa or PLUS debit cards, UK accounts require an institution using Faster Payments, and applicable EU account sections say banks should support receiving SEPA Instant Payments. These are destination-selection rules. The directory records no payout submission, success or settlement transition. Compare old raw lines 4–21, 5671–5677, 6569–6577, 6805–6807 and 7255–7257 with new raw lines 5–20, 5670–5675, 6567–6574, 6795–6797 and 7231–7233. source-stripe-payouts-instant.md is the broader Dashboard guide summary. Its line 65 description of the directory as a US lookup is too narrow in both captures, and the line 49 EU label needs the May guide’s Euro Area qualification.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/instant-payouts-banks, the substantive dated changes are a November 7, 2026 Lead Bank row limited to some US accounts (old raw lines 6254–6261, new raw lines 6252–6260) and a German N26 GMBH debit-card row narrowed from all to some versus May 11, 2026 (old raw lines 7215–7221, new raw lines 7191–7197). Inline tables replacing expandable sections, removed subheadings, and changed Markdown formatting are presentation changes (old raw lines 12–22, new raw lines 13–21). Keep both dated captures and the rail-specific country qualifications, including the UK Faster Payments and EU 'should' language. The identical Bank of America N.A. display label appears with conflicting account classifications in both dates (old raw lines 5687–5689 and 5950–5956, new raw lines 5684–5687 and 5947–5954). Preserve the reciprocal source-stripe-payouts-instant.md and stripe-payouts routes. Correct the summary's US-only directory description separately from the row changes and keep exact institution rows in the dated raw.
